ELPAC Level 1
Lexile 1300–1400L
DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Three Strings, One Night

STS-HS10-L1-13001400-HSELA910-PCI-NAV-01 • HS English 9–10 • Narrative Techniques and Multiple Plot Lines
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Booth Tapes records in diners because a diner is where three different conversations happen at three different tables on the same night, and none of the people know they are in the same story. Rosalie's draft is built that way on purpose: one plot line leaves, one waits, one works the last shift, and all three arrive at the same booth by midnight. The teacher is clipping up the third line before anybody has decided whether it earns its place.
If Rosalie cut the third plot line, what would the other two lines have to do differently for the ending to still land?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Maya doing?
Look at the picture. Name what Maya is doing. Choose the exact word for her action and the word she is showing, not a general word like "thing" or "stuff".
2
What is Desmond holding?
Look at the picture. Name what Desmond is holding. Choose the exact word for the object in his hand, not a general word like "thing" or "stuff".
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Name what the teacher is doing. Choose the exact word for her action and the object in her hands, not a general word like "thing" or "stuff".
4
What place is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Name what kind of place this is. Choose the exact word for the features you are using as proof, not a general word like "thing" or "stuff".
5
Tell me about the cards on the wall.
Look at the picture. Name one thing about the cards on the wall. Choose the exact word for how the cards are hung and what is written on them, not a general word like "thing" or "stuff".
6
What is Rosalie wearing?
Look at the picture. Name what Rosalie is wearing. Choose the exact word for the color and the kind of clothing, not a general word like "thing" or "stuff".
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: CCSS.ELA-LITERACY.W.9-10.3.b — Narrative techniques: dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
